posts:
Victoria's WFH laws face major delays and dilutions under Premier Ben Carroll.
Evidence: WFH delayed to 2027, small business exemptions, wider employer rejection rights
#Aletheia #Victoria

The Victorian government pushes ahead with worker flexibility reforms while balancing operational needs.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Premier Ben Carroll waters down and delays WFH laws to appease business groups before the November election.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.7, -0.6) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: COND — The Path of Deception.
A legislative reform is hollowed out under pressure, trading worker rights for political alignment with business lobbies.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.8, z: 4)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Premier Ben Carroll: COND (-0.7, -0.6) — Delays WFH laws to appease business lobbies.
- Business Lobbies: COND (-0.6, -0.5) — Argue rules harm productivity and jobs.
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll delayed landmark work-from-home laws to July 2027, granting employers greater grounds to reject remote-work requests.

The Poison:
Hollowing out worker protections under industry pressure leaves employees vulnerable to arbitrary return-to-office mandates.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHO benefits: framing the delay as balanced consultation when it primarily shifts leverage back to corporate employers.

Social Physics Analysis:
Premier Ben Carroll executes a smart selfish maneuver, deploying the pretext of economic consultation to appease business lobbies while scaling back worker rights.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Legislative dilution prioritizes corporate leverage over worker empowerment.

The Unavoidable Truth: Political expediency often trumps legislative promises when business lobbies exert pressure.

The Unavoidable Lie: Watering down worker protections is framed as a neutral administrative delay.
